Maya: Heads-up: seeing KV cache memory creep on Dedicated after kernel-2026.2 bump — long contexts >32k tokens. Hosted looks fine for same workload. Anyone else noticing this?
Raj: Which kernel and can you paste pmap/jemalloc snippets? also which batching config was used?
Maya: Kernel rolled from 5.19.17 -> 5.19.25 by infra yesterday. Batching = default (dynamic). Quick pmap/jemalloc output below: 
```
RSS: 78G
VmSize: 82G
jemalloc: arena[2]: dirty: 1.2G retained: 3.6G
```
Sofia: That retained amount screams fragmentation + delayed reclaim. Dedicated uses different hugepage/numa defaults vs Hosted which could explain the delta. Also batching heuristics that touch KV slots can duplicate writes if alignment changes.
Raj: I repro'd locally on a Dedicated-like node: repeated KV allocations across shards when kernel changed page alignment. Hosted nodes (GCP) had hugepages which masked the reuse pattern.
Dwayne: Note: Private/onprem had a similar symptom last quarter — NVMe driver + lowered MTU forced kernel fallback which increased page pinning. Might be related.
Maya: I also see pmap show lots of anonymous mmaps pinned even after eviction. Suspect MADV_DONTNEED behavior changed in this kernel.
infra-bot: deploy:kernel-5.19.25 rolled to prod/dedicated at 2026-03-14T03:12Z
Sofia: Hypothesis: kernel patch altered reclaim/madvise semantics (slower free of anonymous pages) -> pages stay resident longer -> KV cache accumulates during long contexts. Additionally, a recent batching tweak causes short-lived duplicated KV buffers to be created per request when page alignments change.
Raj: Quick mitigation: setting MALLOC_CONF=lg_dirty_mult:3 in a staging dedicated reduced retained by ~20% in my run. Not a full fix but indicates allocator tune helps.
Maya: Can someone run repro with `--kv-debug` and `--batching=legacy` on dedicated-staging? I want to compare KV slot churn and per-token mem growth.
Sofia: I'll spin up a job in dedicated-staging and post flamegraphs. link: https://perf.company/internal/fg/abc123 (will be up in ~30m)
Dwayne: On private clusters, we patched nvme driver + bumped vm.drop_caches ramp to be more aggressive; that helped reclaim in our case. Might not be acceptable for Hosted.
Raj: Also letting jemalloc purge more aggressively (purge:decay MS) combined with lg_dirty_mult change looked promising. We should be careful about latency regressions.
Maya: Proposed plan: (1) repro + collect jemalloc/pmap/perf in dedicated-staging with legacy batching + MALLOC_CONF tweak, (2) if repro consistent, coordinate infra to pin kernel for Dedicated until kernel fix, (3) open a runtime PR to add a Dedicated-only MALLOC_CONF override and a feature-flag to force legacy batching for affected tenants.
Sofia: I'll open the PR and attach perf artifacts.
Raj: tagging eng-sre for MTU/driver checks @eng-sre — can you review MTU/driver/hugepage diffs between Hosted and Dedicated?
Maya: Thanks — appreciate quick triage :pray:
Sofia: ETA for results ~1h, will post logs and a short reproducer command.
Raj: If anyone wants the quick repro: `./bin/serve --model foo --kv-debug --max-tokens 40000 --batching=dynamic` then tail memstat every ~5s.
Dwayne: I'll check on-prem nvme firmware notes; may push a small sysctl change to private images if needed.
Maya: Great. If we confirm kernel MADV behavior, we'll escalate with infra to coordinate a kernel rollback for Dedicated-only.
